audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagree with the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: The mirrored jax__tryndamere audit set both layers to Tryndamere / Jax / Jax / Jax / Skill / Skill / Skill with ratings 3, 7, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5 from its side — the inverse of what this page needs. Level 1 is Tryndamere's outright; levels 2 through 5 belong to Jax once Empower and Counter Strike are online; from 6 onward it is close, at 50.09%.
audit.corrected: Tryndamere, Jax, Jax, Jax, Skill, Skill, Skill — five matched full/content pairs plus ratings, as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the level-6 stage was framed as an unconditional Jax takeover.
audit.why: Counter Strike 17/15/13/11/9s — it is 17s at rank 1 against Spinning Slash's 12s, the widest cooldown gap in the lane, and it closes to 9s by rank 5. Empower 7/6/5/4/3s. Leap Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s. Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90s. Undying Rage 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], spikes[1], whys[3], whys[4], late and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is described only as 'dodges autos + stuns'. What it does not dodge is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Jax's combat prowess allows him to dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies.' It is basic attacks it evades, not ability damage — so the instruction is to stop attacking and let it expire, not to run out of range. On a Fury champion, autos held is Fury not gained, which is the real cost.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not abilities — stop attacking while it is up and let it expire.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' in whys[4], spikes[1] and 'late'. The kit gives Grandmaster-at-Arms.
audit.why: The kit file is the authority on names, and this is the same class of error as 'Ares of Blaze' for Pyroclasm — an outdated name a player will not find in game. The ability is also two effects, not one: magic damage on every third consecutive attack, plus an active that raises Armor and Magic Resist briefly.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster-at-Arms lands magic damage on every third consecutive attack, and its active adds armour and MR for a moment — 110s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Empower's auto-attack reset was absent, and Mocking Shout appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Empower is a 7s reset at rank 1 falling to 3s — the swing is the tell, not a cast. And Mocking Shout's slow only lands on an enemy whose back is turned, so leaving a trade by running is what makes it useless.
audit.corrected: Empower is a 7s auto reset: the swing is your cue to step out. Mocking Shout only slows an enemy whose back is turned.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0], early and spikes[0] refer to Jax's 'dash charges', and spikes[3] to 'E Spinning Slash resets'.
audit.why: Leap Strike has no charges — it is a single 700-range leap on 8s at rank 1, and it can target an ally or a minion. Spinning Slash has no reset either; it needs a target unit, which is why keeping a minion or jungle camp in range is the actual escape plan.
audit.corrected: Spinning Slash needs a target unit — jungle camps and wave minions are your escape route.

edits.before: You dominate level 1 as a strong early duelist against a famously weak-early Jax with no dash charges.
edits.after: You dominate level 1 as a strong early duelist against a Jax with only one ability online yet.

edits.before: You stay ahead at level 2 while Jax still lacks both W and E to trade back safely.
edits.after: At 2 Empower is a 7s auto reset and Leap Strike closes 700 range onto you.

edits.before: At level 3 it evens out once Jax has Leap Strike and Counter Strike to answer your trades.
edits.after: At 3 Counter Strike dodges all your basic attacks for its duration and then stuns.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even as the fight comes down to dodging his stun versus landing your crits.
edits.after: At 4-5 Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1, but Empower falls to 4s and he trades for free.

edits.before: Level 6 tips to Jax: Grandmaster's Might adds resists and a magic proc that out-duels your crit.
edits.after: At 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms adds resists on a 110s cooldown, and Undying Rage answers the burst.

edits.before: At first item Jax's BorK/Sunderer plus stun uptime beats you in a sustained fight.
edits.after: At first item his sustained duel and your crit burst roughly cancel each other.

edits.before: Late game Jax's scaling resistances and reliable stun make the extended duel his.
edits.after: Late he wins the straight duel, but he cannot match your split-push tempo.

edits.before: Jax has E Counter Strike but no dash charges yet if he skills Leap Strike late, so you can trade with Q Bloodlust auto weaving as long as you sidestep the Counter Strike stun window; the trade goes even once he has both W and E up.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not abilities — your autos are what it eats, so stop attacking while it is up and let it expire. It is 17s at rank 1 against your 12s spin, the widest gap you will ever get on him.

edits.before: Jax R Grandmaster's Might swings the duel hard: the passive third-hit magic proc plus the armor/MR bonus means your raw crit output no longer out-DPSes him, so respect all-ins the moment his ult is available.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms lands magic damage on every third consecutive attack, and its active adds armour and MR for a moment — 110s at rank 1. Break the attack chain by stepping out, and take the fight after the resists lapse.

edits.before: Full-build Jax with E stun uptime and R resistances beats you in an extended duel; use your superior split-push mobility with E Spinning Slash resets rather than face-checking him in a bruiser slugfest.
edits.after: Full-build Jax wins the extended duel, so do not take one. Spinning Slash needs a target unit, which means jungle camps and wave minions are your escape route — split where you always have one in reach.

edits.before: From level 6 and items onward Jax overtakes you: Grandmaster's Might resistances and stun uptime beat raw crit in a straight duel, so pivot to split-pushing and picking flanks rather than dueling him head-on.
edits.after: From level 6 on Jax wins the straight duel: Grandmaster-at-Arms resistances and a 9s Counter Strike at rank 5 beat raw crit. Pivot to split-pushing and flanks, and keep a minion or camp in spin range.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Don’t crit into it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Counter Strike (E): 17s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5 — it dodges basic attacks, not abilities. - Empower (W): 7s down to 3s, an auto reset. - Mocking Shout: 14s. - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Dodges autos + stuns. Don’t crit into it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and eats basic attacks only — stop autoing.

edits.before: That is Jax's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Empower is a 7s auto reset: the swing is your cue to step out, not the cast.

edits.before: Track Jax's Counter Strike: Dodges autos + stuns. Don’t crit into it. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows an enemy whose back is turned — leave a trade facing Jax, never running.

notes: The packet's suspectName is a false positive: wants.foe[0] writes 'Land Counter Strike stun…' and Counter Strike matches the kit exactly. Left in place and unverified, as the mirror also flagged: whys[2], spikes[1], early, mid and wants.you[0] on the Jax page claim the Counter Strike stun interrupts Spinning Slash mid-dash. Riot's Spinning Slash text carries no channel or interruptible language and there is no matching flag, so I neither wrote nor removed that claim — but note I did rewrite spikes[0] and spikes[1] here, and neither of my replacements asserts an interrupt.
